admitted_historical_durable_gate_payload.digest_pins_are_an_additional_bind_not_t: The payload is independently cross-checked against the live authority bytes, the live manifest bytes, the manifest's own capture-unit identity set, the authorized capture-critical closure and the re-derived gate-critical closures. Pinning the two durable digests here makes admission strictly stricter; it does not replace any of those checks.

anti_laundering: The admission record names admission_regime HISTORICAL_DURABLE_GATE_PAYLOAD_ADMITTED, which is distinct from both SAME_FREEZE and HISTORICAL_ADMITTED and cannot be produced by either wrapper path.
The record states the historical gate source and the current processing source separately and never normalizes one to the other.
The record states physical_gate_wrapper_receipt_recovered=false and physical_gate_wrapper_receipt_regenerated=false as facts, not as claims of success.
does_not_authorize: re-running the physical gate to obtain a different result
reconstructing, regenerating or writing any physical-gate receipt wrapper
claiming the original wrapper survived, or claiming this successor produced the gate
admitting a gate over a different cohort, manifest, or authority
admitting a FAIL, BLOCKED or incomplete gate under any commit
any change to raw captures, capture receipts, or the frozen scientific design

lost_wrapper.destroyed_by: SageMaker Space host rebuild wiped /mnt/sagemaker-nvme in full
lost_wrapper.exhaustive_search: No object matching this digest exists anywhere under the campaign durable prefix, and no physical_gates*.json exists anywhere on persistent local storage. The derived namespace stores payload plus checksum manifest and never stored the wrapper; there is no unit_state record for stage2_physical_gates.
lost_wrapper.must_never_be_regenerated: Rebuilding a wrapper around the surviving payload and calling it the original receipt is FORBIDDEN. This authority admits the payload AS a payload. Nothing may claim the wrapper survived, and nothing may write a local physical_gates.json.

principle: The wrapper is a SERIALIZATION. The gate RESULT is the payload. Every condition the wrapper admission rule tests is either carried by the surviving payload, carried by the surviving checksum manifest, or re-derived from source -- except the wrapper's own digest, which is exactly the thing that was lost and is therefore never asserted. Admission is granted on the same load-bearing condition as wrapper admission: GATE-CRITICAL CLOSURE EQUALITY at the gate's source commit and at the current processing source. It is refused on anything else.
question: The local physical-gate receipt WRAPPER was destroyed by a host rebuild. Its durable PAYLOAD and checksum manifest survived, immutable, in the campaign's own durable namespace. May a Stage-2 processing successor admit that surviving durable evidence instead of the lost wrapper, WITHOUT re-executing the physical gate and WITHOUT reconstructing the wrapper?
required_conditions: the durable checksum manifest reproduces its pinned digest
the durable payload reproduces its pinned digest
the checksum manifest's own files entry for payload.json equals the payload digest
the checksum manifest authority sha256 equals the live authority bytes
the checksum manifest manifest sha256 equals the live manifest bytes
the checksum manifest scientific run id equals the manifest run namespace
the checksum manifest unit id equals the manifest physical-gate unit
the checksum manifest source commit equals the named gate source commit
physical_gates.required_checks equals the gate implementation's own check vocabulary
physical_gates.capture_units equals the authority scientific capture count
physical_gates.paired_trajectories equals the authority trajectory identity count
the payload per-unit cohort identity equals the manifest capture unit identity set exactly
the payload cohort capture-critical closure equals the authorized capture-critical closure
all admitted capture closures were equal when the gate ran
the payload's recorded processing_source_commit equals the checksum manifest source commit
the gate source commit resolves in this repository's Git history
the gate-critical closure at the gate source commit equals the gate-critical closure at the current processing source
the current processing source is not the gate source commit, which is what makes this the historical regime
